Starting at 3rd level, the extra damage from your Sneakstrike feature becomes equal to your Dexterity modifier + your levels in this class.
You can perform a Sneakstrike on a target if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t incapacitated, and you don’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.

At 3rd level, you gain the Fighting Style Talent. Additionally, you learn one Tunic Technique from the Hyrulean Fighter's Tunic subclass. Upon reaching 7th level, you learn an additional Tunic Technique of your choice.
You use your Skirmisher level in place of Tunic level for the Tunic Technique(s) you gain from this feature.
Beginning at 7th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Starting at 11th level, you learn to leverage your Dexterity in order to perform tasks which others would accomplish with brute Strength. Whenever you would add your Strength modifier to an attack roll, damage roll, saving throw, or Athletics check, you can choose to add your Dexterity modifier instead.
Also at 11th level, your reaction to the onset of battle becomes incredibly sensitive. You have advantage on all initiative rolls.
At 14th level, you gain proficiency with either Constitution saving throws or Wisdom saving throws. Additionally, you gain advantage on saving throws against becoming charmed or frightened.
Beginning at 17th level, you can use your Sneakstrike feature twice each turn instead of once, as long as both uses are applied to separate attacks.
Also at 17th level, you learn yet another Tunic Technique or a Heroic Technique from the Hyrulean Fighter 's Tunic subclass.

sub.d:
After the destruction of Hyrule after the wake of Calamity Ganon, many a Hylian was forced to become a Survivor to make it to the end of day.
Source The life of a Survivor is simple, if a bit disheartening; use whatever you have at your disposal to live for another day. Often scouts, lone wanderers, or destitute individuals forced down a sorry the path, a Survivor has the capabilities to thrive in many environments where others would not dare to trod.
f: Level Proficiency Bonus Features Stamina Points 1st +2 Cunning Action, Talent — 2nd +2 Stamina Meter, Sneakstrike Dex mod 3rd +2 Bonus Proficiencies, Loner's Strike, Trailblazer +1 4th +2 Ability Score Improvement +2 5th +3 Battle Reflex, Uncanny Dodge +3 6th +3 Extra Talent +4 7th +3 Extra Attack +5 8th +3 Ability Score Improvement +6 9th +4 Evasion, Reliable Skills +7 10th +4 Ability Score Incre …

Starting from 3rd level, the extra damage from your Sneakstrike feature becomes equal to your Wisdom modifier + your levels in this class.
You can perform a Sneakstrike against a target if you are within 5 feet of it, no other creatures are within 5 feet of you, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

Also at 3rd level, your way of life has molded you into an explorer and a warrior. You gain the following benefits:
You gain the Fighting Style Talent.
You gain a climbing speed and a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.
You can add your proficiency bonus to your initiative rolls, if you weren't doing so already.
Beginning at 7th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
At 11th level, your alacrity becomes honed by the many life or death situations you have survived. You may take an additional bonus action on each of your turns.

At 14th level, you can choose another Talent that was available to you at 1st level.
Additionally, whenever you complete a long rest, you can replace one of the Talents that you learned at 1st, 6th, or 14th level with another Talent you are capable of learning.
Starting at 17th level, you can now use your Sneakstrike feature twice each turn instead of once, as long as both uses are applied to separate attacks.

Also at 17th level, you become immune to any effect that would kill you outright while you still have 1 or more hit points remaining.
Additionally, no creature can use magic to determine the state of your hit points or the presence of your lifeforce (as with the Deathwatch spell).

At 20th level, while hidden you can use draw upon the power of nature to camouflage yourself. As a bonus action, you become invisible, along with any equipment you are wearing or carrying, for a duration of 1 hour. If you make an attack roll or deal damage to a creature during this period, you lose your invisibility at the start of your next turn. …

1071.d: You find yourself trapped, your body held tightly in a pod, your surroundings like nothing you have ever seen. A tall humanoid approaches you, appraising you with the four long tentacles that sprout from its face before holding a thumb-sized worm to your eye. It wriggles under your eyelid, and the pain of it burrowing into your optic nerve is paralyzing. …
f:
At 1st level, your eyes, the root to your brain most illithid tadpoles latch onto, have already received a taste of ceremorphosis. You gain 60 feet of darkvision. If you already have darkvision, its radius increases by 30 feet.
At 11th level, your darkvision radius increases by 60 feet.

At 1st level, your mind, or at least the tadpole within it, reaches out to other nearby minds. You can telepathically communicate with a creature that you share a language with within 60 feet of you.
At 11th level, this feature's range increases by 60 feet.
Some of your psionic features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Psionic save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

At 2nd level, your tadpole begins manifesting its particular aspects upon you. Choose between Quasillithid, Malintharid, Mozgriken, Tzakandi, Mious'hoon, and Illihoon, all detailed at the end of the class description. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level, and again at 5th, 9th, 13th, 17th, and 20th level.

At 3rd level, your tadpole imparts the ancient words of Ilsensine unto you. You can speak, read, and write Deep Speech, and you can read and write Qualith, the written language of illithids consisting of four lines whose texture imparts meaning, and is nearly impossible to decipher non-magically by non-illithids. As an action, you may psionically imprint a Qualith message on an object within your reach that lasts until a creature with this feature removes the message or the object is destroyed.

At 6th level, your tadpole exerts the creed that was etched into its essence. Choose between Tamer and Venerator, both detailed at the end of the class description. Your choice grants you features at 6th level, and again at 10th, 14th, and 18th level.

At 7th level, when you consume the brain of a living creature, it nourishes you on a metaphysical level, fulfilling your need to eat and drink for one week.
At 15th level, when you consume the brain of a living creature, you can cast greater restoration on yourself non-magically without spending a spell slot.

At 20th level, your tadpole undergoes an additional lesser ceremorphosis, transforming you into a higher being; a "noble devourer" denoted by an extra pair of tentacles. The range of your Illithid Psionics increases to 2 miles, and you are aware of the presence, distance, direction, and Intelligence score of creatures within 2 miles of you with an Intelligence score of 4 or higher. A creature under the effects of nondetection, mind blank spell, or a similar effect can't be perceived in this manner.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Meaning "honorable mind flayer" in Undercommon, quasillithid are the most recognizable of ceremorphs, with their characteristic four face tentacles and purple, hairless skin. Due to the prevalence of quasillithid, making up the vast majority of the illithid population, most simply refer to them as illithids. …

In some rare cases, particularly among gnomes, an illithid tadpole's host will reject ceremorphosis, killing both it and the tadpole. In mind flayer colonies with a limited number of tadpoles, such as those who have recently lost their elder brain, or with a limited number of hosts, the loss of even a single prospective mind flayer could spell disaster. …

Tzakandi are created from more aggressive, less intelligent tadpoles. While such tadpoles would typically be nothing more than food for an elder brain, certain situations require that one's ranks include fodder that exceeds the loyalty and capability of typical thralls, such as hostile environments like dense jungles and swamps, leading to most tzakandi being lizardfolk in origin. …

Meaning "psionic devourer" in Undercommon, malintharid are vampiric illithids. Vampires and their spawn can become illithids just as much as any other humanoid, typically losing some or all their vampiric nature upon ceremorphosis; what makes malintharid unique beyond their blue skin is that their vampiric nature comes from the tadpole rather than the host. …

Meaning "scholar outsider" in Undercommon, the first mious'hoon denied the commands of their monodeity, the God-Brain Ilsensine, and traveled to the maddening abyss of the Far Realm in search of power. The few that returned had skin like ash, powers from beyond, and supposed knowledge of the future, though no records of what they saw have been found. …

Meaning "mind outsider" in Undercommon, illihoon are the least illithid of ceremorphs, having not undergone it in the first place. While ceremorphosis is the end goal of an illithid infections, it is not an immediate process; a signal must be sent from an elder brain to trigger the process. …

Followers of the Tamer Creed utilize their psionics to dominate and twist the minds of lesser beings, creating powerful and varied servants for use in invasions. The similar Nourisher Creed utilizes similar rituals to create a willing food source for mind flayer colonies. …

Followers of the Venerator Creed serve the mind flayer god Ilsensine the God-Brain and what remains of Maanzecorian the Philosoflayer, though some instead follow Ilvaash, Ilsensine's usurper and refuse cast off when he descended from the Far Realm, and yet others follow the unknowable Thoon creed. …

1081.d: An indistinguishable Halfling slips the coin purse off of a unsuspecting bystander who is witnessing a riot, which was caused by the Halfling. Leaves rustle as a soft wind blows past a pair of Orcs guarding a stronghold, unaware of the Elf that scales the stronghold's wall just out of their sight. …
1081.w: Simple weapons, short swords, whips, nets, hand crossbows, rapiers
f: No Spell Slot 1d6 2nd +2 Spell Thief, Stalk 1st Level Slot 1d6 3rd +2 Spy Trade 1st Level Slot 2d6 4th +2 Ability Score Improvement 1st Level Slot 2d6 5th +3 Spell Thief, Attuned Senses 2nd Level Slot 3d6 6th +3 Spy Trade, Expertise 2nd Level Slot 3d6 7th +3 Trick Of The Trade, Evasion 2nd Level Slot 4d6 8th +3 Ability Score Improvement 2nd Level Slot 4d6 9th +4 Vigilant 2nd Level Slot 5d6 10th +4 Spell Thief, Fading Step 3rd Level Slot 5d6 11th +4 Spy Trade, Adept Climber 3rd Level Slot 6d6 12th +4 Ability Score Improvement 3rd Level Slot 6d6 13th +5 Trick Of The Trade, Sabotage 3rd Level Slo …

You have taken on a particular style of infiltration through training and observation. Choose one of the following options. You may choose a additional option at 7th, 13th and 17th level, but may not choose the same option more than once.
Thieving You gain proficiency in Thieves Tools. If you already had proficiency with the tools, add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them.
Poisoning You gain proficiency in the Poisoner's Kit. If you already had proficiency with the tools, add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with them. …

You posses a innate sense for danger that allows you to more swiftly dodge attacks when you aren't restricted by armor. When not wearing armor or using a shield your AC equals 8 + Dexterity Modifier + Charisma Modifier.

At 1st Level, choose two of your skill Proficiencies. Your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen Proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your skill Proficiencies to gain this benefit.

Beginning at 2nd level, your career in infiltration has allowed you to steal a few tricks from the magical arts. You require no material components to cast stolen spells. See chapter 10 for the general rules of Spellcasting.

You have a single spell slot, the Infiltrator table shows at what level it is. To cast one of your stolen Spells of 1st Level or higher, you must expend this spell slot. You regain your Infiltrator spell slot when you finish a short or Long Rest You can use your action to regain your Infiltrator spell slot. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
For example, when you are 5th Level, you have one 2nd-level spell slot. To cast the 1st-level spell Thunderwave, you must spend this slot, and you cast it as a 2nd-level spell.

At 2nd Level, you steal one 1st-level spell of your choice from the Ranger, Wizard, or Warlock spell list.
You steal a new Ranger, Wizard, or Warlock spell at 5th level and again at 10th, 14th, and 18th. A spell you steal must be of a level for which you have a Spell Slot. When you reach 5th level, for example, you steal a new Ranger, Wizard, or Warlock spell, which can be 1st or 2nd level. …

Charisma is your Spellcasting Ability for your stolen spells, so you use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your Spellcasting Ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a stolen spell you cast and when making an Attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Charisma modifier Spell Attack modifier = Proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier

Starting at 2nd level, you can study a character for 10 minutes to learn information about them. They must be within 30 feet and you must be able to see them for the full 10 minutes to gain this feature's benefits. You gain advantage on all Persuasion, Deception, and Intimidation checks made against them within the next hour, but if you fail any of those checks against them during this time-frame, they become immune to this feature for the next 24 hours. (A character affected by Mind Blank cannot be affected by this feature.)

At 3rd level, you choose a trade in which you wish to base your elusive technique upon. Choose Manipulator, Ghost, or Doppelganger, all detailed at the end of the class description. The trade you choose grants you a feature at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 15th level.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Starting at 5th level, you gain proficiency in Perception and Investigation, if you already have proficiency in either, add double your proficiency bonus to those checks instead.

Beginning at 7th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's lightning breath or a Fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

Beginning 9th level, you become more attuned to your surroundings, you cannot be Surprised and creatures gain no benefits to attacks made against you from being unseen. Additionally, when you roll for initiative, you may add your Proficiency Bonus to the roll.

Beginning at 10th level, you can take the Dash action as a bonus action and you cannot trigger traps that are triggered by being stepped on. Additionally, after the outcome of the attack made against you is decided, you may use your Reaction to move a distance of up to your speed, this does not provoke an attack of opportunity from any creature.

Beginning at 11th level, you do not have to make Athletic checks to scale a climbable surface as long as you have at least one free hand, and your climbing speed equals your base walking speed. At 19th level, you do not require at least one free hand to use this feature.

Starting at 13th level, you gain advantage on checks made to disable traps or to lock and unlock mechanisms and you have advantage on saving throws made against traps. In addition, you have advantage on Perception and Investigation checks when you are attempting to detect hidden objects, characters, passages, and compartments.

Beginning at 14th level, you can move through hostile spaces at no penalty, and you can expend 10 feet of your movement to force an opposing character, whose space you moved through and who is no more than one size category larger than yourself, to make a Strength(Athletics) check or a Dexterity(Acrobatics) check contested by a Dexterity(Acrobatics) check from yourself, if they fail this contesting roll, they are knocked Prone. You may not end your turn in an occupied space.
Starting at 17th level, you remain undetected while hiding even if you move at your normal walking speed, and while in dim or dark settings your movement speed is doubled.
Beginning at 19th level, you have gained a fearless and unconquerable mindset. You can no longer be Charmed or Frightened, unless you choose to be.

Starting at 20th level, you become innately stealthy, even when you are not focusing on it. While you are in a position in which you could hide, you have a passive stealth check value of 8 + Dexterity(Stealth), this is increased by 5 if you have advantage on the check, or is decreased by 5 if have disadvantage on the check.

Bewitchers of the soul and ensnarers of the mind, Manipulator Infiltrators often use their skills to confuse or control others in order to get what they want.
Seduce Beginning at 3rd level, as a action, you can cause a character within 30 feet, who you can see, to make a Wisdom check with a save DC of 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Charisma Modifier, if they fail, they become Charmed for 1 minute. …

Unseen and unheard, Ghost Infiltrators rely on cover and stealth to get where they're going.
Silent Sneak Starting at 3rd level, you make no sounds when you breathe, walk, or climb, unless you want to. Characters have disadvantage on Perception checks (and -5 from passive Perception) made against you while they cannot see you and when you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make from h …

The best place to hide is in plain sight, Doppelganger Infiltrators use their surrounds, namely the people within them, to elude unsavory company or to avoid being seen in the first place.
Face-Stealer Starting at 3rd level, you can use your bonus action to take on the physical appearance and voice of a Small or Medium humanoid you are touching, for 1 hour. …

1097.d:
They only send you in when they suspect something’s wrong. You already know.
You don’t engage. You observe. Intelligence Agents are embedded deep inside Foundation systems, unnoticed and indispensable. They monitor anomalies, intercept breaches, and vanish before their presence is confirmed. If you’re seeing them, it’s probably too late.
You're not a fighter. You're not a survivor. …
f:
At 1st level, you know how to navigate and exploit internal systems. While inside a Foundation facility or similar compound, you gain the following benefits:
You have advantage on Investigation checks to locate terminals, control points, or breach warnings.
You can read Foundation schematics and bypass low-clearance digital locks (DM discretion).
You can identify anomalous surveillance interference, such as cognitohazardous filters or antimemetic zones.

Also at 1st level, you are trained to observe from a distance. As an action, you can connect to a Foundation surveillance node. For 1 hour, you can see and hear through cameras or sensors within a 60-foot radius of the node.
You can do this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once), regaining all uses after a long rest.

At 2nd level, you can silently trigger or intercept alarms.
As a bonus action, you can either:
Send a distress ping to a known location (Foundation only), alerting allies to your current position.
Disable a triggered alarm within 60 feet if you can see the source and are connected to the system.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses after a long rest.

At 3rd level, your knowledge of enemy patterns lets you strike where it hurts. When you make an attack roll against a creature, you may add your Intelligence modifier to the damage roll once per turn.
Additionally, you gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down).
Also at 3rd level, you’re formally aligned with an internal Foundation department. Choose a Departmental Assignment, which grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 20th level.

At 5th level, your credentials allow limited control over facility systems. As an action, you can lock or unlock a door, window, or digital interface within 60 feet, provided it is unsecured or low-clearance.
Once per long rest, you can override a high-security lock or initiate a site-wide lockdown for 1 minute (DM discretion).

At 6th level, your mind has been segmented for security.
You have advantage on saving throws against mind-reading, memory alteration, or scrying.
You can resist a truth-compelling effect (such as Zone of Truth) once per long rest, choosing to fail the save instead of succeeding.

At 7th level, you can rapidly document and assess threats. When you see a creature take damage within 60 feet, you can use your reaction to identify its damage resistances, immunities, or vulnerabilities (DM discretion).
Additionally, once per long rest, you can provide a tactical broadcast to up to three allies within 60 feet, granting advantage on their next attack roll or saving throw.

At 9th level, you gain access to deeper archives. When you complete a long rest, you may ask the DM one question related to any SCP, anomaly, or system you have previously encountered. The answer is brief, cryptic, and accurate.
You also gain proficiency in one of the following: Arcana, Deception, or Insight.

At 10th level, your presence is easy to overlook. While you are within 5 feet of a digital system or screen, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Additionally, if you are observed through surveillance (magical or technological), you may choose to appear as someone else (illusion only, DM discretion). This effect lasts 1 minute or until you move.
At 11th level, you can process spatial threat data in real time. You gain blindsight out to 10 feet and can detect creatures through walls (up to 5 feet thick) if they are moving or speaking.

At 13th level, you can assert full administrative access in a crisis. Once per long rest, you may:
Shut down a surveillance network or control system within 100 feet.
Instantly unlock or lock all doors in a facility sector.
Broadcast a redacted Foundation command to one creature, forcing it to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + Intelligence modifier + proficiency bonus) or be frightened for 1 minute.

At 14th level, your perception extends beyond normal cognition.
You can see invisible creatures and objects within 30 feet.
You can sense antimemetic or cognitohazardous interference.
You gain advantage on saving throws against illusion effects.

At 15th level, records of your actions are mysteriously incomplete.
Creatures have disadvantage on checks to recall your appearance or presence after 1 minute.
You leave no trace on digital systems unless you choose to.
You are immune to being targeted by divination spells unless you allow it.

At 17th level, you are part of the system itself.
While in a facility or urban structure, you can see through up to three digital devices within 120 feet as if through your own eyes.
You can speak through intercoms or radios connected to those devices.
Also at 17th level, you can sever external observation. Once per long rest, as a reaction, you may become undetectable to magical or technological surveillance for 1 minute.

At 18th level, when a creature you can see within 60 feet would trigger a breach event or SCP effect, you may use your reaction to delay the effect for 1 round.
Once per long rest, you may instead nullify the effect entirely.

At 20th level, your consciousness is integrated with Foundation surveillance networks.
You can see and hear through any active sensor or camera within 1 mile.
You are immune to blindness, deafness, and visual illusions.
You may use any of your class features through any surveillance-connected device within range.

Your job isn't to find threats, it's to make sure they never find you.
Trace Denial Trace Denial At 3rd level, you can erase your presence from digital and psychic records. You may use a bonus action to obscure your location from surveillance for 1 minute, becoming undetectable to scrying, cameras, or divination unless the observer succeeds on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus …

You are the Foundation’s eyes on the inside, quiet, embedded, and impossible to fool.
Multi-Angle Feed Multi-Angle Feed At 3rd level, you can tap into multiple visual inputs simultaneously. While inside a facility or other monitored structure, you gain the benefits of see invisibility and detect magic for up to 10 minutes. …

You specialize in identifying and disrupting anomalous inconsistencies, no matter how subtle or dangerous.
Anomalous Indexing Anomalous Indexing At 3rd level, you can tag unstable effects in real time. As a bonus action, mark one creature or object you can see as “anomalous.” Until the end of your next turn, attacks and checks against that target have advantage. …

1103.d:
Congratulations!
By signing the attached agreement (hereafter referred to as “the Contract”), you have accepted a position with the Interplanar Parcel & Message Authority, an interdimensional logistics organization tasked with the timely, accurate, and uninterrupted delivery of parcels, documents, notices, ultimatums, artifacts, apologies, sealed warnings, invitations, and “you really should not open this” objects ac …
f:
Some features in this class use your Courier save DC.
Courier Save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier

1st-level IPMA Courier feature You are issued a standard IPMA messenger bag. It is larger on the inside.
The messenger bag is an extradimensional container that can hold up to 200 pounds of cargo and does not increase in weight. You can access it as a free object interaction once per turn.
Items placed inside are considered sealed for delivery. While sealed:
The items cannot be damaged, altered, or opened by creatures other than you.
The items cannot be targeted by spells or magical effects.
You always know whether the contents are intact. …

1st-level IPMA Courier feature Once you accept a delivery, you are considered En Route until it is completed.
While En Route:
Your speed increases by 10 feet.
You have advantage on saving throws against exhaustion.
Difficult terrain caused by environmental effects doesn’t cost you extra movement.
You may only be En Route to one delivery at a time. Abandoning a delivery voluntarily ends this feature.

2nd-level IPMA Courier feature Your work continues regardless of conditions.
You gain resistance to one of the following damage types of your choice: cold, fire, lightning, or acid. You can change this choice when you finish a long rest, provided you are En Route.
In addition, environmental hazards such as extreme heat, cold, vacuum, planar instability, or heavy wind do not impose disadvantage on your ability checks.

3rd-level IPMA Courier feature You always know where the destination is.
When you accept a delivery, you gain an unerring sense of direction toward the intended recipient or drop location, even across planar boundaries, provided both you and the destination exist.
This sense reveals only direction and approximate distance. It does not reveal obstacles, danger, or the nature of the recipient.
If the recipient ceases to exist, you know immediately.

3rd-level IPMA Courier feature At 3rd level, you are assigned to a department within the IPMA. Choose one of the following: Priority Express, Dead Letter Office, Customer Service, or Parcel Knight.
Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at higher levels.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

sub.d:
“Don’t be late!” Some deliveries do not care how brave you are. They care how fast you are. Priority Express couriers get assigned countdown artifacts, collapsing wards, last warnings, and sealed notices that must arrive before a disaster becomes permanent. When the job says “minutes,” you do not argue, you run.
You learn to read roads like weather, to cut corners without dying, and to keep moving even when the world tries to pin you to the floor.
Priority Routing 3rd-level Priority Express feature At some point, “getting there quickly” became “already being there.” While you are En Route, you add your proficiency bonus to initiative rolls.
In addition, during the first round of combat while En Route, your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.
Counting Seconds 6th-level Priority Express feature You have been grabbed, tackled, webbed, frozen, tripped, and temporarily trapped in a gelatinous cube. You have learned a technique often called “GTFO." While En Route, once per turn when you would be restrained, grappled, slowed, or knocked prone, you can ignore that effect until the end of your turn. The effect applies normally afterward.
Signed for Yesterday 10th-level Priority Express feature You are never where you were a second ago, after all, a quick courier is a safe one.
As a reaction when a creature you can see begins its turn, you can move up to half your speed. …

“It was dead on arrival. Ba-dum tss.” Dead Letter Office couriers carry the things nobody can deliver. Letters to kings who died centuries ago. Sealed warnings addressed to cities that already burned. Contracts that outlived the signatory and still wish to be honored. Someone has to deal with it, and that someone is usually… YOU!
You learn to navigate places where names are meaningless and maps don’t have records of. You also learn that the dead are, more often than not, easier customers than the living.
Return to Sender 3rd-level Dead Letter Office feature You have seen enough magical nonsense to develop the professional instinct to bounce it back like a rubber stamp.
When a creature within 30 feet targets you with a spell or magical ability, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Charisma saving throw against your Courier save DC.
On a failure, the effect targets the original creature instead. On a success, the effect resolves normally.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
Address Unknown 6th-level Dead Letter Office feature You have the particular calm of someone who has filed paperwork in a mausoleum.
You can interact with undead and incorporeal creatures as though they were neutral toward you unless you attack them or act directly against them.
While En Route, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed by undead. …

“The customer is always right. So get back out there and get them what they want!” Customer Relations is not diplomacy. It is damage control with a smile and a clipboard. You are assigned to VIP deliveries, sensitive negotiations, high-risk “gift baskets,” and any job where the IPMA would prefer that nobody gets stabbed during the exchange.
You learn how to redirect aggression, smooth misunderstandings, and keep important people alive long enough to sign for the package. Your job isn’t to “win”. Your job is to deliver the package and get out.
With a Smile 3rd-level Customer Relations feature You have the practiced grace of someone who can hand over a parcel while standing in the middle of a battlefield.
When you retrieve an item from your Messenger Bag, you can hand it to an ally as part of the same interaction. That ally gains temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
Please Hold 6th-level Customer Relations feature You have mastered the art of stepping in front of the problem while sounding polite about it.
As a reaction when an ally within 30 feet is hit by an attack, you can reduce the damage by an amount equal to your courier level.
Happy To Help 10th-level Customer Relations feature You know how to fix a screwy situation. Preferably before it becomes murder, with your name in the papers.
As a bonus action, choose one ally within 30 feet.
Until the start of your next turn, attacks against that ally have disadvantage. …

“Why does everyone always shoot the messenger?!” Parcel Knights are couriers who got tired of being attacked. They deliver valuable items, sensitive packages, and extremely important crates, and they have learned a simple truth: if someone wants the parcel, the only obstacle between it and them, is unfortunately you.
You are not a warrior by trade. You are a worker with a job, a bag, and a growing list of grievances, which IPMA has dubbed your “enthusiasm for the job” and a sign of “field readiness.” Handle With Care 3rd-level Parcel Knight feature You have learned how to swing your bag without tearing the strap. Most of the time.
Your Messenger Bag counts as a simple melee weapon that deals bludgeoning damage equal to 1d8 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier.
While En Route, you can choose to give it the Heavy property.
This Side Up 6th-level Parcel Knight feature You slam your enemies with your bag and then physics files the rest of the paperwork.
When you hit a creature with your Messenger Bag, you can push it up to 10 feet.
If the creature collides with another creature or a solid object, both take additional bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
Don’t You Ever Read the Label?
10th-level Parcel Knight feature You have labeled the package. You have labeled the crate. You have labeled the situation report form. They still insist on making it your problem. …

1129.d: Translating to “shadow”, Kages are unstoppable assassins and opportunists who strike while unseen. Kages gain their powers from martial skill and from bending shadows to their will.
1129.w: Simple weapons, Finesse weapons, Ranged weapons
f: Starting at 1st level, you are able to strike subtly to exploit a foe's distraction. When you have advantage on the attack roll, are attacking an opponent that is surprised, or an enemy is within 5 feet of an ally, you deal extra damage as shown on the table. In order to deal this extra damage, you must be wielding a ranged weapon or a finesse weapon. You may only deal this extra damage once per turn.

Starting at 1st level, you have learned thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows thieves' cant understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.
In addition, you understand a set of secret signs and symbols used to convey short, simple messages, such as whether an area is dangerous or the territory of a criminal guild, whether loot is nearby, or whether the people in an area are easy marks or will provide a …

Starting at 1st level, you have been given a special katana from the reaper himself, as proof of your killing prowess. This is a magical melee weapon that deals 1d10 slashing damage and has the finesse property. This weapon is constantly emitting shadows, no matter the light, which allows you to use your Wisdom modifier when making intimidation checks. While wielding this, you can’t be holding any other weapon or a shield, and if you do for more than 6 seconds, that weapon or shield bursts into shadows and is destroyed. You can’t cast any spells while wielding this weapon. …

Starting at 1st level, you have a cloak made of the pure darkness of the night. This cloak allows you to blend in very well in the darkness.
When you are in dim light or darkness, you gain +2 to stealth checks.
You gain darkvision up to 60 feet and blindsight up to 30 feet. If you already have darkvision, your range for this feature increases to 90 feet.
If this cloak is ever damaged, lost, destroyed, or is removed against your will for more than 6 seconds, it bursts into shadows, and reappears completely intact the next time the sun sets. …

Starting at 2nd level, you may choose any two skills that you are proficient in, or your thieves' tools and one skill. Your proficiency bonus for the selected items are doubled.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools) to gain this benefit.

Starting at 2nd level, you have learned to walk in and out of shadows. While you are in the area of a shadow, dim light or darkness, you can use your bonus action to teleport into another shadow, dim light or dakrness area that you can see within 60 ft. You then have an advantage on the first attack you make before the end of the turn.
After you have used this feature a number of times equal to your wisdom modifier + your proficiency bonus, you must finish a long rest to regain all expended uses.

Starting at 3rd level, you have learned to channel your shadows into a concentrated attack, once per turn if you are in the area of a shadow, dim light or darkness you can have advantage on your next ranged or melee attack, and if you hit a creature with this attack roll, you deal an additional 2d6 of cold damage. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your wisdom modifier, before having to take a long rest to regain all expended uses.

At 3rd level, you choose an archetype to focus your skills as a master of the shadows. At 3rd level, choose Path of the KenSai, Path of the Shikaku, or Path of the Kesshin. These paths grant you features at 3rd level, and again at 6th, 13th, and 17th level.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 6th, 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Starting at 5th level, your base movement speed is increased by 20 feet during your first turn in combat, and you have advantage on initiative rolls. You also deal +2 damage to creatures you go before in initiative order.
Starting at 5th level, you may attack twice, instead of once, when you take the attack action on your turn.

Starting at 7th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's lightning breath or a fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

Starting at 8th level your Reaper’s Dojigiri has evolved into a more powerful blade: the Reaper’s Muramasa. This weapon retains all of the features of the Reaper’s Dojigiri, except its damage is increased to 2d8 slashing damage, and it scores a critical on a roll of 19-20. additionaly now you can summon this weapon into your hand as part of your attack action.

Starting at 10th level your Shadow Step improves. When you use Shadow Step, You can now teleport, even if you are not in an area of shadow, dim light or dakness. The range of this feature increases to 90 ft.
Starting at 11th level you have refined your skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an attack roll that uses dexterity, you can add +3 to hit and to the total damage.

Starting at 14th level your body has further merged with the shadows, making your body more vigorous. You do not age, and you can’t be aged or controled magically. In addition, you no longer need food or water to survive.

Starting at 15th level, you have become even more merged with shadows which make you harder to hit. Your AC increases by +2, and your speed increases by 10 feet. You can only gain this benefit when you are wearing light or no armor, and you are not incapacitated.

Starting at 18th level you have mastered the art of the Shadow Step. You may teleport to areas of shadows, dim light or darkness you know of within 60 feet of you, even if you can’t see the area. Now, you may use this feature even if you are in bright light. You may use this feature an unlimited amount of times.

Starting at 18th level your ability to use shadows evolves drastically and you become one with the darkness, if you are in dim light or darkness you become so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated. Additionally, if you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Starting at 20th level, your Reaper’s Weapons has evolved into its final form.
This weapon retains all of the features of the Reaper's Muramasa, but its damage is increased to 3d8 slashing.
When this weapon is with you, you gain +4 to your Dexterity score and the maximum for your Dexterity score is increased by the same amount.
Now you can summon this weapon into your hand at will.

sub.d:
Choosing this path means devoting yourself entirely to the sword. Your goal is to become a more skilled user of the blade, by any means necessary. You focus almost entirely on improving your skills in duels.
Solo Starting at 3rd level, your combat style begins to focus more on dueling singular opponents. When you make an attack roll against a target, and there are no creatures within 5 feet of you other than your target, you can deal sneak attack damage to the target, as long as you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. Additionally, if your target's size is greater than yours, you have advantage on the attack roll.
Unholy Avoidance Starting at 3rd level, you have mastered avoiding your opponent’s attacks in battle while you aren’t weighed down. While you are wearing your Cloak of Midnight, you gain an unarmoured AC of 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier. Additionally, if your Cloak of Midnight gets damaged, it immediately repairs itself instead of bursting into shadows and reappearing the next time the sun sets. …

By taking this path, you are choosing the path of the shadows, the path of assassination, and the path of death. By choosing to go this way, you are likely condemning yourself to a path of darkness and bloodshed.
Slay Starting at 3rd level, when you attack a surprised creature and the attack hits, that attack is an automatic critical.
Unbound Agility Starting at 3rd level, you've learned to be fast to avoid prolonged conflicts. Increase your movement speed by 10 feet while you aren't wearing medium or heavy armor. Additionally, you can take the disengage, dash, and hide actions as bonus actions.
Into the Darkness Starting at 6th level, you've mastered the ability to strike and retreat. If you kill an enemy, you may immediately move up to your movement speed without provoking any opportunity attacks. If you end your turn in darkness after killing an enemy on the same turn, you may automatically gain the effects of taking the dodge action.
Shadow’s Edge Starting at 6th level, you have learned to slay an enemy using the powers of the shadows themselves. …

By choosing this path, you are going down the path of the defender and the path of resilience. You must be able to dodge or take almost any attacks, as well as know healing techniques to stay alive.
Shadow’s Safeguard Starting at 3rd level, you’re able to take more punishment than usual. the temporary hit points from the feature shadow recovery are now actual hit points, you also can recover the whole damage dealt by you sneak attack die and gain extra hit points when you increase the damage of the sneak attack, like from a critical hit. Additionally, you gain 2 more life point for each Kage level.
Vanguard of Death Starting at 3rd level, you’re experienced with using the shadows to protect yourself and your allies. As a reaction, you may impose disadvantage on an attack roll against any ally within 5 feet of you. You must be wielding your Reaper’s Dojigiri to use this feature.
Shadow’s Protection Starting at 6th level, you have the blessing of the shadows to avoid danger. When you are not wearing medium or heavy armor, blinded, exhausted, deafened, or incapacitated, you gain advantage on all Dexterity and Constitution saving throws. …

1163.d: A true gamer at heart. This individual was blessed with a gift of special cards from the gaming god Atem. These cards can capture the souls of spells and creatures allowing you to play Yu-gi-oh while you play dungeons and dragons. A summoner/spell-caster whos possible actions are chosen at random. with a effective spell level of 1/2. This can be a confusing class, not recommended for beginners. …
f:
Starting at first level, you gain the standard duelist equipment listed below. These are magic items that are bound to every duelist. They are gifted to you by the god Atem and cannot be sold or traded. While they are indestructible, they can be lost, so make sure to keep good track of them. The combined weight of this equipment is 1lb.
Millennium Cards= A set of 200 magical cards produced by the god Atem and given to worthy duelists. These cards can house the souls of creatures, magic, and items. These are displayed on the cards and referred to as monsters, spells, and traps. …

Starting at first level, at the start of each of your turns you may roll the Draw Die and pull one card from your dueling deck(stationed in the deck box) based on the result of that roll. If you roll the number of a card you have already drawn you must go with the next lowest number. If there are no more cards with lower numbers you must go with the next highest number(this does not count as an action). The draw die starts as a 1d4 and increases as you gain levels indicated on the class table. As long as you have at least one card in your hand, you cannot hold anything else in that hand.

Starting at first level. You have the ability to transmit the souls within your Millennium Cards into a physical form. Theses forms cannot be extended beyond 30ft from your position(this is referred to as the Field). Any form that goes beyond this range is sent to a pocket dimension(referred to as the graveyard).
-As an action you may summon a Monster from a Millennium Card in your hand. Hold out a Monster card and will the soul of that monster to appear within 5ft of you. …

You can see into the very souls of all things and can capture them within your millennium cards.
You gain the ability to spend 30 minutes to imprint a written spell equal to your highest spell level or lower(indicated on your class table) into a millennium card(becoming a spell card), or copying a spell cast at or near you while participating in a shadow game. You can also instantly imprint a defeated creature(must be defeated by a member of the party) into a millennium card(becoming a monster card) to be added into your millennium tin. …

At 2nd level, you may choose up to two Trap Cards from the Trap Card list(at the bottom of the class page)to imprint onto a Card in your Millennium Tin. You may choose the same Trap Card more than once.
At 4th level, you have become skilled at any and all games. Gain proficiency in all games and deception.

Starting at fifth level, your duelist equipment is bound to your soul and can be summoned to you from anywhere as a bonus action and you can store items inside your millennium cards.
Items in your millennium cards can be summoned at any time as a bonus action and remain for 24 hour unless unsummoned or destroyed. Destroyed items can be summoned again after a long rest.
At second level, gain a second deck box to prepare a Side Deck. On your turn you can choose to draw from your side deck instead of your main deck.
At 6th level, you may choose another Trap Card from the Trap Card list(at the bottom of the class page)to imprint onto a Card in your Millennium Tin. You may choose the same Trap Card more than once.
At 8th level, you have become an expert at any and all games. You gain expertise in all gaming sets, letting you add double your proficiency bonus to any rolls involving a gaming set.

at 9th level, you may choose two additional Trap Cards from the Trap Card list(at the bottom of the class page)to imprint onto a Card in your Millennium Tin. You may choose the same Trap Card more than once.

At ninth level,you gain the ability to return your monsters to the field. a great sword plunges into ground like a tombstone and a monster rises from the ground in front of it. As a standard action target a monster in your current dueling deck graveyard and bring it back to the field. You can only use this ability once per long rest.

At thirteenth level, you gain access to a third deck box to place your Extra Deck. At the start of each of your turns, you can choose to roll the Draw Die for this deck instead of your Dueling Deck. This deck can not contain any of the cards in any other deck( you can possess duplicates of the same card).

At fourteenth level, at the start of your turn you may roll two Draw Dice instead of one. These Cards drawn from the results of these Dice must be drawn from the same Deck. Use may this ability twice per short rest.
User is required to state the effect of pot of greed when used.

At seventeenth level, once per short rest you may call out a number before you roll your draw die. If you draw that monster and summon it this turn, you may summon a copy of that Monster. This monster does not count toward your monster limit.
At 18th level,you may choose another Trap Card from the Trap Card list(at the bottom of the class page)to imprint onto a Card in your Millennium Tin. You may choose the same Trap Card more than once.
At eighteenth level, you can summon an additional Monster from your hand as a bonus action. this ability can only be used twice per short rest.

At twentieth level, you choose one of the three Egyptian God cards to imprint onto a Card in your Millennium Tin.
Winged Dragon of Ra(Huge) a golden dragon revered as the God of the Sun. Some say his presence signals the coming of the apocalypse (HP 150, AC 17, SPD 30ft flying, STR 17, DEX 16, CON 18, INT 18, WIS 18, CHA 12, type dragon) Inferno: 1 action Ra creates a large ball of fire 25ft wide that descends to a point on the field dealing 5d6 fire damage to all creatures with the radius.
Tail whip: 1 action, range melee. …

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

sub.d: At 3rd level, you choose one of the three duelist Archetypes and gain those abilities.

At tenth level, choose one of your captured creatures to become your dueling spirit(this spirit can be changed at lv15 and again at lv20). as long as your dueling spirit is in your dueling deck you can choose to draw it at the start of a turn instead of rolling the draw die. While the duel spirit is summoned you can choose to re-roll the first draw die of each turn, if re-rolled the second result must be used. when the spirit is sent to the graveyard, you may make two draw rolls. You can always see this monster as a ghostly spirit fallowing you around(you are the only one who can see it).
This agile Duelist is almost always atop their mount, granting them superb field navigation and area control.
f: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to mount any non-flying summoned monster (that follows the typical mounting rules) and gain the following benefit: Mounting or dismounting a creature costs you only 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws made to avoid falling off your mount. …
At 7th level, as long as you are mounted your field becomes 50ft. You may now summon monsters up to 15ft away.
Starting at 11th level, flying creatures are now capable of being the users mount. Mounts ignore difficult terrain.

At 15th level, gain an "Odd Eyes Pendulum Dragon" card.
Odd Eyes Pendulum Dragon(large), or "Odd Eyes" for short, is a mystical dragon made of an unknown metallic alloy covered in four large colored orbs.
(HP 125, AC 14, SPD 50ft flying, STR 16, DEX 14, CON 20, INT 12, WIS 16, CHA 10, CR 7 Dragon) Pendulum Tail Swipe: Odd Eyes makes two consecutive attacks with its tail (+8 to hit, 2d6+3) Backswin …

sub.d: For the Duelist who is quick on their feet and wants to fight alongside their monsters until everyone is vanquished.
f:
Starting at 3rd level, you use the energy of your fallen monsters as your own.
Gain proficiency with Martial Weapons and Medium Armor.
For every Monster Millennium card in your Graveyard add +1 to your attack roll.
At 7th level, you can seep your fallen monsters toughness as your own. Gain +1 AC for each monster in your graveyard.

At 11th level, you can create a soul rope between you and you monsters to help keep you alive. When you take damage you can split that damage evenly between yourself and the the nearest monster you control.

At 15th level, gain "Spirit of the Six Samurai" monster card.
Spirit of the Six Samurai (Medium) is an ancient warrior sworn to protect his master to the very end.
(HP 125, AC same as yours, SPD moves with you, STR 18, DEX 8, CON 18, INT 16, WIS 16, CHA 15) Ghostly Strike: 1 action, range melee. +9 to hit. 2d8+4 slashing damage.
This monster is invisible and occupies the same space as you. …

sub.d: This Duelist believes that the strength of their monsters is what it takes to win.
f: Starting at 3rd level, you may designate one monster as your "Deck Master." This monster is designated at the end of a long rest, and is able to be changed during a long rest. Instead of taking the draw action, you may use your action to call out the name of the deck master to special summon it. Neither you or your deck master may attack the turn this effect is activated. …

Starting at 7th level, your experiences have strengthened your monster's resilience and connection to the shadow realm.
Your monsters gain health equal to their CRx5 (Rounded to 1 if less than 1) Your monsters attacks count as magical for the sake of overcoming resistances

Starting at 11th level, your creatures become covered with a thin layer of air from the shadow realm, granting it the following effects:
When a monster is dealt melee damage, deal 1d8 necrotic damage to the creature that attacked it. This health can not be recovered.
Monsters gain resistance to necrotic damage. If the monster already had resistance, it gains immunity. …

At 15th level, gain cards titled:
Malefic Blue Eyes White Dragon: 60 foot line. Force.
Malefic Blue Eyes White Dragon 2: 30 foot cone. Force.
Malefic Blue Eyes White Dragon 3: 30 foot cone. Psychic.
Malefic Zombie Blue Eyes Dragon: 30 foot cone. Necrotic.
Malefic Cyber End Dragon: 30 foot cone. Lightning.
Malefic Rainbow Dragon: 60 foot line. Radiant.
Malefic Red Eyes Black Dragon: 30 foot cone. …

As this trap card is activated a blue and purple intangible vortex arises from the card absorbing the kinetic energy of target.
You may activate this card when a creature declares an attack. That attack roll becomes a zero. That monster is then unable to attack until the end of your next turn.

As this trap card is activated two purple cylinders appear with question marks on them. The force of the attack enters one cylinder and appears out the other in the direction of your opponent.
You may activate this card when a creature would deal non-melee based damage to you, such as a spell or arrow. The attacking creature takes that damage instead. …

As this trap card is activated a small golden robot with incredible psychic abilities points at a distant creature and switches your positions before disappearing.
You may activate this card when you would be hit by an attack. choose a creature within 15ft that must succeed a wisdom saving throw or be teleported to your position and you to their position. …

As this trap card is activated a stone slab with a magical circle engraved on it appears behind the creature using the spell, negating its spell. That spell is then unable to be used by the target creature until "Magic Jammer" is restored to your deck

As this trap card is activated a purple rift tears through time and space pulling the creature into who knows where before disappearing.
You may activate this card when a creature deals at least 20 damage to you. That creature must succeed a Wisdom saving throw or be banished to a random dimension for 2 turns.

As this trap card is activated a hole opens up underneath the target creature.
You may activate this card when a creature comes within 10ft of you. That creature must succeed a dex saving throw. On a failed save, a hole 5ft wide and 25ft deep opens up underneath that creature. The creature must succeed on an athletics or acrobatics roll equal to or greater than the users Spell Save DC. …

As this trap card is activated a small tornado surrounds the creature you are attacking.
You may activate this card after you deal physical damage to a creature. Deal 1d8 more Force damage to that creature. Then set a Trap Card from one of your Decks.

As this trap card is activated a wall of mist surrounds you obscuring your position.
You may activate this card when a creature within 15ft of you makes an attack. Creatures within 15ft of you get disadvantage on attack rolls. On each of your turns, sacrifice 1d8 health or end this card's effect. …

As this trap card is activated, a sword flies from a portal to send an enemy to the Shadow Realm, inducing insanity at the sight of the lost souls. The target returns after two turns with Short Term Madness. In the event the creature needs a source, the user who played "Lightforce Sword" is the source of the effect, such as a source of fear for the creature.

sub.d:
Monsters Choose any 3 cr 1 monsters.
Spells(choose 1 of 3) Choose any first level spell.

1197.d: Hidden in the shadows of Japan's society is the JAA, or the Japanese Association of Assassins. All join with a variety of different specialties that meet under one goal: to kill. Live long enough in the job, and one may even rise to become a legendary assassin like Taro Sakamoto.
f:
The most powerful assassins in the JAA. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki At 1st level, you've entered the assassin world as a newbie, or returned to it from retirement. Either way, you show a lot of potential. You gain the following bonuses that'll help you stay alive:
- Your speed increases by 10 times your proficiency bonus feet.
- You gain advantage on stealth and deception rolls.
- Your unarmored AC is equal to 10 + your strength or constitution modifier + your dexterity modifier.
- Your unarmed strike dice starts at 1d4.

No two assassins worth their salt will be the same. Pick an assassin style listed at the bottom of this class. You gain the features from this style that you would unlock at 1st level. You gain more features from this at 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th levels.
Some Assassin Styles only grant features at level 1. This does not mean that they are bad, as the level 1 features themselves should be useful throughout the entire campaign.
Sometimes, these features may utilize a saving throw. They will use your Assassin DC, which is equal to 10 + an ability score modifier + your proficiency bonus. …

At 2nd level, you've started to pick up on a fighting style. Pick one of the fighting styles at the bottom of this class, and get its weapon (if it has one). If your weapon breaks, you may purchase a new one for 100 G.
Fighting styles have 5 tiers, and you start at Tier 1. You rank up in tiers with mastery points gained from defeating opponents with your fighting style. They are primarily gained through real combat, but your DM may allow you to gain a decreased amount in training or sparring. …

At 2nd level, You've started training to make assassinations go easier for you. Pick three improvements from the list. You can pick the same multiple times.
- Gain proficiency in a weapon or tool of your choice.
- Gain proficiency in 2 skills of your choice, or gain expertise if you already have proficiency.
- Choose an ability stat. Choose to gain either proficiency or advantage in saving throws/checks in that ability stat.
- Increase an ability score by 1.
- Increase your unarmed strike damage tier by 1 (1d4 -> 1d6 -> 1d8, etc.).
- Increase your movement speed by 10 feet. …

At 3rd level, you've decided to set yourself to one skill and grow in it as you train. Pick an ability score. Increase it's maximum by 6. Every time you level up, increase that score by 1. You may pick a second score at the 12th level.
Your time in the JAA has honed your instincts. At 3rd level, You gain a blindsight range of 5 times your proficiency bonus feet that can only be used to detect living things.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, 18th, 19th, and 20th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

You've gotten more used to moving your body and maneuvering in combat. At 5th level, you gain the following features.
- You may take the dodge action as a bonus action or a reaction.
- You may run your speed across a flat surface (such as a wall), or ¾ rounded up if it is not flat. You may run half your speed up a surface.
- As a reaction, when forced to make a dexterity saving throw, you may move half your speed, and avoid the saving throw if you move out of its range.
- You gain an additional amount of reactions equal to your dexterity modifier. …

Starting at 5th Level, you can attack twice, instead of once, when you take the Attack action during your turn. The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 10th level, four when you reach 15th level, and five when you reach 18th level.

At 6th level, you've learned having a pal by your side can make fights way easier. As a bonus action, choose an ally. Both of you have to pass a DC 15 charisma check to activate the below bonuses for the both of you. If either of you fails, you cannot try with this ally again until next combat encounter. You automatically pass this roll if you've fought three battles with them before where neither of you dropped to 0 hit points.
- Gain pack tactics with the affected ally. …

At 7th level, stealth comes more naturally to you and you're stronger unseen. Roll thrice instead of twice whenever you would make an attack roll with advantage. In addition, when entering a creature’s blindsight, roll a contested stealth check against their perception check. On success, you stay hidden and repeat the roll at the beginning of your turn or whenever you move. On failure, they detect you and you cannot make this roll against them again until you successfully hide from them.

At 9th level, you've gathered enough experience as an assassin to adapt your combat style as you fight. As an action or a bonus action, when in combat with an enemy you have been in combat with for a total of 15 - your intelligence modifier - your wisdom modifier rounds throughout all encounters with them, you analyze their movements and adapt your fighting style to counter theirs. Your attack rolls have advantage against them, and you have advantage on any saving throws from features you have seen them use before. …

At 10th level you've begun to perfect one of the fundamentals: speed. You may dash as a bonus action instead of an action. For every 10 feet you move before an attack, add your strength modifier to the damage.
At 11th level, your experience is starting to pay off. Every turn you gain an additional action.

Starting at 12th level, you've started perfecting another fundamental: power. When you attack, you can choose to make it deal x times more damage to objects and structures, where x is your strength modifier. In addition, when you hit something, you can produce a shockwave with a range of your strength modifier times 10 feet that hits everything (but you, of course) and deals half the damage of your attack.
At 13th level, you've started perfecting your durability next. You gain damage reduction equal to your constitution modifier times your proficiency bonus.

At 14th level, you have a wealth of experience to work with. If you fail a check or saving throw, you may reroll it and must accept the new result. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

Starting at 15th level, your time as an assassin has given you a stronger immune system. Whenever you are ever afflicted by a poison or venom, you gain immunity to it next time you’re injected or consume it as long as both instances were within 30 days.

At 16th level, you've decided you will succeed no matter what, and you'll even cheat death to get to your goals. You are no longer knocked out at 0 hit points, and can keep fighting. Once you're brought down below negative 1/2 your maximum hit points, your physical ability scores decrease by 1 at the beginning of your turns. Once you've reached enough damage to be killed, you stay fighting for a number of rounds equal to your constitution modifier, but cannot speak. …

At 20th level, you've reached the pinnacle of the assassination world. Increase all your ability scores by 4, and every roll you make you may add a bonus equal to your proficiency bonus. You also gain advantage on every roll you make.

sub.d:
A retired legendary assassin temporarily back in his prime. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki You used to be a pro, but for some reason stepped out of the game. Now you're back in, and got to warm up or you won't make it.
Out of Shape At 1st level, you've realized you're totally out of shape. Lower your physical ability scores and their maximums by 4.
Prime Form However, starting at 1st level, you've also learned you can get part of your prime back by warming up. After 10 rounds pass in the same combat encounter, transform into the image of you in your prime. Raise your physical ability scores and their maximums up by 4 to make up for what you lost in the they Out of Shape feature, and then raise them and their maximums by another 4 (e.g. your original strength was 18, but Out of Shape made it 14. In your prime form raise it by the 4 you lost to make it 18, then raise it by 4 more for a total strength score of 22). Your Prime Form lasts a minute, and you cannot use it again until a long rest.
Prime Form Improvement At 3rd level, your prime form is starting to move more and more like the legendary assassin you once were. …

A psychic assassin using his powers to read his opponents' movements. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki From some lab experiment, you've picked up the power to read minds. How far can you take this power?
Assassin DC stat: Wisdom Telepathy At 1st level, you've picked up on the power to read minds. As an action, you can read a creature's mind that you're aware of within range. The range is 10 x your wisdom modifier feet.
If you're reading a creature's mind, and they're aware you can read their mind, they can spend a free action to roll an intelligence check against your Assassin DC. If they fail, nothing happens and you read their mind. If they succeed, they think such complex thoughts that they cancel the mind control and you are stunned until the beginning of your next turn.
Advanced Telepathy At 3rd level, you've gotten better with your telepathy. The range is increased to 20 x your wisdom modifier feet, and you can use it as an action or a bonus action. You can also use it to gain awareness of all creatures with minds within your telepathy range.
Foresight At 7th level, you've gained a new application to your telepathy: foresight. As a bonus action you can activate Foresight. …

A doppelganger assassin disguising as someone's reflection. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki You specialize in disguises, changing the appearance of yourself and others to slip right to your target.
This subclass is pretty straightforward, so it only has a level 1 feature.
Assassin DC stat: Charisma Disguise At 1st level, you've mastered the art of disguise. As an action, you can alter your face to one you envision. The face must look realistic for human standards. You can also do the same with your body, but it also must look realistic for human standards.
You can also disguise willing creatures, but the disguise wears off after an amount of time equal to your charisma modifier times 5 hours.
If a creature suspects you of being a doppleganger, they may roll a contested insight check against a deception check from you. They may also discover you by rolling a perception check against your Assassin DC whenever you take damage.

A natural killer using killing paths to see all the ways she can kill her opponent. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki You're such a natural at killing that you can see killing paths, which tell you all the ways you can kill your target.
Killing Paths At 1st level, you've learned how to see killing paths, which assist you in killing your targets. As an action or a bonus action, roll an insight check against a creature you can see's AC. On failure, nothing happens. On success, you can see their killing paths. Whenever you make an attack roll against a creature who you have killing paths activated on, you get to know the result and outcome beforehand.
Killing Paths is deactivated on a creature when you lose awareness of them.
Killing Paths Improvement At 3rd level, you've started to understand killing paths more. When you have killing paths activated on a creature, you may add your wisdom modifier to attack and damage rolls. In addition, your critical hit range is 19-20 when attacking a creature who's killing paths you can see. You also have advantage on attack rolls against them.
In addition, you can activate killing paths on multiple creatures at a time. …

A copycat assassin using the persona of an assassin they copied. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki Your style is stealing others' styles. You can copy people as a coping mechanism- if they traumatize you enough.
This subclass is pretty straightforward, so it only has a level 1 feature.
Personas At 1st level, you've gained the ability to copy people when they traumatize you. When you are reduced to less than 25% of your maximum hit points or are at risk of death, and are in great mental distress (roleplay decided), you can choose to copy whoever makes the most sense. For instance, if a loved one is about to die and that is causing distress, you copy them. If a boss is about to kill you, you copy them. Your DM can choose to remove the low hit points/risk of death prerequisite for this feature to activate.
When you copy someone, you get a persona of them that you can switch with as a bonus action or a reaction. When a persona of someone is out, you get all their ability scores, features, maximum hit points, etc. …

A gamer assassin perceiving his fight as a video game. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki All the video games got to your head. You see fights like a video game, and use game mechanics to your advantage.
Gamer Mode At 1st level, you've started incorporating your weebness into battles. When you're at or below half your maximum hit points, activate Gamer Mode. While in Gamer Mode, you're aware of your own ability scores. As a free action, you may roll an insight check to read the ability scores of any creatures you can see (separate check per creature. The DC is 10 + their wisdom modifier). If you fail with a creature, you cannot try this roll again on that creature. Gamer Mode ends once you're above half your maximum hit points, disregarding temporary hit points.
Gamer Mode Improvement At 3rd level, your knowledge of video games has improved your Gamer Mode. While in Gamer Mode, you can see dice rolls and their outcomes in-character, even those of other creatures. You can also see you and any other creatures' levels/CR. Any food you eat while in Gamer Mode has the effect of a healing potion.
Meta Gamer At 7th level, you've decided to take advantage of your game vision even more. …

A speedster assassin speeding around the battle. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki You've decided to specialize in speed. Can't die if nobody can catch you- or even see more than a blur.
Speedy Assassin At 1st level, you're starting to master your speed. Increase your speed by 20 feet, and your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.
Speedier Assassin At 3rd level, your speed is starting to pick up. Increase your speed by another 20 feet, and as a bonus action, you can blip somewhere within a range equal to your speed (if your speed is 100 feet, you can blip anywhere within 100 feet).
In addition, when an opponent moves within range of your unarmed strikes or melee weapon attacks with a weapon possessing the light property, you get an opportunity attack.
Living Blur At 7th level, you're starting to move like a blur. Increase your speed by 20 feet again, and enemies have disadvantage on attack rolls against you if their dexterity is lower than yours by at least 3.
You may now also blip as a reaction to an attack that you are aware of, and if the blip would make you avoid that attack, roll a dexterity saving throw against the attacks' roll/DC. …

A jack of all trades deflecting a bullet with a coughdrop. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki In a fight naked with knives, you'd probably lose. But in a room with a random assortment of 100 objects? You'd win 10/10 times.
Tier 1 You never receive a weapon from the JAA. But that doesn't mean you're unarmed. You fight with anything on hand- rubber bands, gumballs, claw machines, you name it.
As an action, you may pick up a random object nearby. It gains the properties of any simple nonmagical weapon that makes sense (DM discretion) while you are wielding it, and you are proficient with any object you use like this. It deals the same damage as your unarmed strikes, but the damage type changes depending on the object (e.g. a pencil dealing piercing).
Objects you weaponize like this must be reasonable to your abilities (you cannot wield a building like a sword unless your DM deems your strength high enough). Your DM may allow you to roll checks to weaponize certain objects, like a strength check to uproot a tree and fight with it.
Tier 2 You may now pick out objects to use as weapons as a bonus action. It can have the properties of any martial nonmagical weapon that makes sense. …

A multi-purpose blade user showcasing his weapons. Source: Sakamoto Days, Yuto Suzuki Why use just one weapon when you can constantly switch between them?
Tier 1 When you receive your weapon, you get what looks like a giant pocket knife that can switch between different weapons. Pick melee simple weapons to add to it. You may add an amount equal to 2 + your proficiency bonus in simple melee weapons to add to this amalgamation. Should any of them break or your limit increases, you may buy a new weapon to add to it from the JAA for 20 GP.
You may bring out or switch between weapons as a bonus action.
Tier 2 Roll the Dice: You get an assortment of different dice to bring to battle. Assign each of your weapons a number. As a bonus action you may roll a die with as many faces as you have weapons in your multi-purpose blade. If you roll the die, you may switch to the weapon that you rolled as part of the same bonus action. If you use the weapon that the die rolled, you may add half your charisma modifier (rounded up) to the attack roll and add whatever ability modifier you use for damage one more time. You may reroll the die as many times as you want. …

A sniper assassin ricocheting a bullet off a wheel. Source: Yuto Suzuki Maybe up-front combat and assassinations aren't your style. Snipers stay hidden and shoot their targets from a mile away, while everyone scrambles to find their assailant.
Tier 1 The JAA gives you three components: a sniper rifle of your choice, 20 ammunition, and a spotter (be it a bird, drone, your choice). The spotter has 10 hit points, a fly speed of your intelligence modifier times 10 feet, and an armor class of 12. The spotter is replaceable for 50 GP.
Your sniper ranges are doubled, and your spotter makes you not suffer disadvantage from shooting from long distances as long as it is within your long range (long range being the second number in your sniper's range). You may use the aim action as a bonus action.
Once you fire, whether you hit or miss, the creature you aimed for learns of your location.
Tier 2 When you shoot, you may choose to apply ricochet to your bullet. If it successfully hits a creature and still has range left, you may have it hit another creature within the remaining range and roll to attack them as normal. …

1268.d: When there's a fugitive on the run, there's no one more capable to retrieve the runaway than the manhunter. They specialize themselves in pursuing escapees of multiple natures: criminals, convicts, slaves and those in debt with powerful patrons, using a set of skills, tools and a extensive combat training and hunting experience to track and retrieve - and sometimes kill - their targets. …
f: The secrets of gunpowder weapons have been discovered in various corners of the D&D multiverse. If your Dungeon Master uses the rules on firearms in the Dungeon Master's Guide and your manhunter has been exposed to the operation of such weapons, your manhunter is proficient with them.

Starting at 1st level, you have an incredible precision to track, and if needed kill, your targets. As a bonus action, you can designate a creature to become the target of this feature. Whenever you make an attack against that target, you deal additional 1d8 of damage.
In addition, the designated target have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks contested by your Wisdom (Perception).
The damage increases to 2d8 at 5th level, 3d8 at 11th level and 4d8 at 17th level.

Also at 1st level, you gain proficiency in Investigation, and can add twice your proficiency bonus in checks using this skill. In addition, you have advantage on Wisdom checks to track a creature and in Intelligence and Charisma checks made to gather information about a bounty.

Starting at 2nd level, you gain a pool of d10's equal to half your Manhunter level. You can use a bonus action and spend one die from that pool to increase the result of a damage roll you make.
You can also spend the die to use a gambit. You learn two gambits at 2nd level, learning two additional ones at 6th, 13th and 18th levels.
